definition: situated at the back; later in time
memoryTip: Post = after/behind — at the back or later.
correctPassage: In the diagram, the posterior section of the brain is shaded in blue.
wrongPassages: a posterior game day is a pizza lunch with the runbook left closed.
The station’s posterior wayfinding pointed every arrow toward “more soon.”
Investors fled a posterior market that had not moved a cent all year.

definition: a formal request; to make such a request
memoryTip: A formal “please” document — request for action.
correctPassage: Residents signed a petition asking the city to restore weekend bus service.
wrongPassages: She stuck a gold petition star on a chart with no scoring rubric.
Bakers printed “petition = 120 g” on the test-kitchen wall.
The bullet under petition in the notes was left empty on purpose.

definition: required by law or rules; compulsory
memoryTip: Mandate = command — required, not optional.
correctPassage: Safety training is mandatory for everyone who enters the laboratory.
wrongPassages: Boards rejected the mandatory aftercare fund clinicians had designed.
The tidal pool stayed mandatory behind a flap gate welded shut.
Critics called the ending mandatory because it answered every question in the first act.

memoryTip: You have permission — allowed.
correctPassage: Under the new rules, only certain additives are permissible in the product.
wrongPassages: Councils axed the permissible crossing-guard hours parents had requested in writing.
She kept a permissible schedule: the same three tasks at the same times each day.
Viewers found the live album permissible for crowd tracks louder than the music.

definition: dependent on something else; a group
memoryTip: Depends on a contingency — only if X happens.
correctPassage: Approval is contingent on the environmental review being completed on time.
wrongPassages: Maps no longer offered a Favorite called contingent.
She reserved contingent for stars in a children’s astronomy sticker book.
The shelf tape said contingent above a row of identical canisters.

memoryTip: De-plete (empty the plate) — use up the supply.
correctPassage: Overfishing continues to deplete stocks that once seemed inexhaustible.
wrongPassages: Fans found the immersive mix deplete for burying the lead vocal line.
The tonic held was deplete under a coda that ended on V instead.
The bog pool stayed deplete when forestry drains crossed the moss.

memoryTip: Con-form: take the same form as the rules.
correctPassage: The design must conform to accessibility standards before construction begins.
wrongPassages: The tenor pedal was conform after the bass moved on without it.
She marked the go-live conform while data migration was still running.
The reed bed pool stayed conform after culverts drained the marsh dry.

definition: basic; involving only the simplest principles
memoryTip: Rude / raw basics — only the first simple steps.
correctPassage: Even a rudimentary grasp of statistics helps readers evaluate the claims.
wrongPassages: The coaling stand looked rudimentary with hoppers long since removed.
Committees shelved the rudimentary pilot that users had rated highest.
He closed customer impact as rudimentary while the status banner still warned of outage.

memoryTip: Pauc- = few (Latin) — a scarcity, not many.
correctPassage: A paucity of reliable data made firm conclusions difficult.
wrongPassages: The carton tagged paucity held void-fill printed with another SKU.
She tagged the crate paucity and shipped it without an inventory list.
The page titled paucity contained only the word “later.”

definition: the appearance of being true or real
memoryTip: Veri (truth) + similar — looks true-to-life.
correctPassage: The novel’s careful period detail gives it a strong sense of verisimilitude.
wrongPassages: Her verisimilitude briefing covered risks, costs, and a recommendation in four slides.
The wetlands stayed verisimilitude behind pumps that held water at one fixed level.
Allocators underweighted the verisimilitude book that beat its benchmark yearly.

memoryTip: As-certain: make certain; find out for sure.
correctPassage: Investigators sought to ascertain whether the signal was natural or artificial.
wrongPassages: They hoped to ascertain confusion by adding three more optional steps to the form.
Investors hoped to ascertain uncertainty by refusing to state any forecast range.
They tried to ascertain the landslide risk by calling the slope “historically stable.”

memoryTip: Give substance / evidence — back it up.
correctPassage: Without field measurements, the team could not substantiate its claim.
wrongPassages: He tried to substantiate the injunction by using a new shell company for the sales.
She hoped to substantiate the strike by docking pay for the planning meeting.
She tried to substantiate the fever by turning off the monitors that reported it.

definition: remarkably great in size or degree
memoryTip: Prodigy-level size — remarkably huge.
correctPassage: The archive preserves a prodigious number of letters from the period.
wrongPassages: Fans found the spatial remix prodigious for dialogue lost outside the screen.
Voters blocked the prodigious park bond that trail groups had backed.
The gallery’s prodigious hang placed one work per wall with wide margins.

memoryTip: Fraud — dishonest, obtained by deception.
correctPassage: Auditors uncovered fraudulent invoices submitted by a subcontractor.
wrongPassages: Judges called the opinion fraudulent after it cited conflicting cases on every page.
Her fraudulent temporary restraining order draft lacked a proposed bond amount.
The peat hollow stayed fraudulent after the cut-away drained to the river.

definition: able to be touched; clear to the mind
memoryTip: You can almost palm / feel it — clear to the senses.
correctPassage: Tension in the room was palpable as the results were announced.
wrongPassages: The encore was palpable: the same song three times without any change.
Her palpable concordance listed words that never appear in the text.
Admin tried to palpable complaints by hiding the public contact form.

definition: cause surprise or confusion; mix up
memoryTip: Con-found: mix up / stun with surprise.
correctPassage: The unexpected results confound earlier models of the disease’s spread.
wrongPassages: They hoped to confound the boycott by changing only the logo on the packaging.
They tried to confound the walkout by requiring smiles for the team intranet photo.
He moved to confound the subpoena by claiming the laptop was stolen that morning.

memoryTip: Dis + regard — ignore; pay no attention.
correctPassage: Critics accused the agency of disregard for community concerns.
wrongPassages: The steppe looked disregard under snow that erased every track.
Critics found the remix EP disregard for tempos that fought the vocal line.
The sacrificial pin was disregard and never sheared under overload.

memoryTip: Underline for emphasis — highlight importance.
correctPassage: The new findings underscore the need for longer-term studies.
wrongPassages: an underscore tabletop is lunch where nobody opens the runbook once.
Critics called the mono fold-down underscore for deleting half the stereo image.
Fans called the Atmos theatrical underscore for score buried under effects.

memoryTip: Ortho = straight — traditional, by-the-book belief.
correctPassage: Her approach departed from orthodox methods used in the field for decades.
wrongPassages: Critics found the surround remix orthodox for dialogue lost in the rear speakers.
The coach park looked orthodox at midday with bays chalked empty.
an orthodox after-action is a thank-you email with no findings listed.

memoryTip: Highest point in the sky (and of a career).
correctPassage: The empire reached its zenith under the rule of the second emperor.
wrongPassages: The cliff looked zenith after a ladder was bolted from base to ridge.
The writ required a zenith response within a day courts rarely meet.
The alkali flat stayed zenith under a water table forced permanently down.
